You are already safe in high-sec space unless you do something exceptionally unwise, like AFK-mining in an untanked T2 mining barge in highly-populated areas or carrying a huge amount of value in ships without the proper defenses through trade choke points where you might get suicide-ganked. This is generally not something you'll need to worry about for many months after you start playing.

If you're venturing out of high-sec, then you should accept that with the increased rewards of more lucrative economic opportunities will come additional risks from player competition. The game revolves around a naturally-balancing equation of risk and reward, which gives value to all player actions.

Also, this is an open-world game. Nothing's stopping you from paying other players for protection, or joining strong groups and getting access to better space in exchange for the contribution of some of your time and/or output.

Your best bet will still always be to just not get into trouble in the first place.

If you want a fleet of players watching your back you'd be best served getting into a nullsec corporation. Their players are organised in a standing fleet and will protect the space you are in and respond to defend you directly if you are attacked, so long as you speak up and survive long enough for them to get to you of course.

This is provided to you at no additional cost to the 10% tax you'd pay in most corporations. Their mining opportunities are also lucrative compared to what you'd find in low sec.

These groups will also replace any ship you lose in group pvp in sanctioned operations and provide you with replacement ventures, destroyers and even T1 cruisers you might lose under any circumstance.
